readme:
# 实例判别：Binary NCE 与记忆库


## 1. 问题


实现 `instance_nce_loss` 和 `update_memory`。非参数实例判别为每张训练图像保留一个记忆库条目，当前查询与正实例及噪声样本进行比较。原论文采用二元噪声对比估计（binary NCE）；候选 softmax 的 InfoNCE 是另一种目标。


## 2. 核心公式


设查询为 $q_b$，候选 ID 为 $j_{bt}$，配分常数 $Z>0$ 固定，温度为 $T$，从 $N$ 个条目均匀抽取 $K$ 个噪声候选：
$$a_{bt}=q_b^T v_{j_{bt}}/T-\log Z-\log(K/N),$$
$$L=\frac1B\sum_b[\operatorname{softplus}(-a_{b0})+\sum_{t=1}^K\operatorname{softplus}(a_{bt})].$$
第 0 列为正例。所有 $a=0$ 时得到 $(K+1)\log2$。记忆更新为 $v_i\leftarrow\operatorname{normalize}(m v_i+(1-m)q_i)$。


## 3. 公式到代码


从 `memory.detach()` 取候选，点积后减去固定 `log_z` 和噪声先验的对数。在对数域用 softplus 保持稳定；K 个噪声项求和，再对 B 个查询求平均。不能把 `K/N` 改为 `1/N`，也不能忽略 Z；整体平移模型对数似然会改变 binary NCE。记忆更新返回独立、脱离梯度的副本。


## 4. 本题约定


查询 `[B,D]`、记忆 `[N,D]`、候选 int64 `[B,K+1]`，K≥1；浮点数据有限且 dtype/device 一致。编码器通常先归一化，但本损失直接使用输入值，不额外归一化。`log_z` 为固定有限 Python 标量；官方一次性估计 Z 的步骤不在范围内。均匀噪声可重复抽取，也可碰到正实例。损失仅对查询回传梯度。记忆更新 ID 必须互异，动量在 `[0,1]`，范数下界默认 `1e-12`；未选中行保持原样，零混合向量保持为零。


即使 momentum 为 1，选中条目仍需归一化；返回值始终拥有独立存储，即使数值无需更新。

## 5. 交互图与 CPU 实验


六个六维归一化实例向量执行 80 次 SGD，学习率 `.35`，T=`.2`，固定 Z=`exp(5)+5`，记忆动量 `.95`。每次枚举另外五个合成实例作为噪声候选，是确定性教学日程，并非复现原始随机采样。实验调用两个待实现函数；T3 要求损失低于 `.8` 且低于初值的 40%，查询与自身记忆平均余弦大于 `.99`，记忆保持单位长度且无梯度。没有图像编码器或下游指标复现。


## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 延伸与来源


与 InfoNCE 的候选分类比较，可以看到二元“数据还是噪声”分类依赖校准后的似然尺度。与 MoCo 比较：MoCo 对编码器做动量更新并维护 FIFO 队列，本方法按数据集实例 ID 更新固定记忆条目。本题对数域公式与数学 binary NCE 等价；不加入官方概率分母中防止数值异常的微小 epsilon，以保持给定概率的精确含义。记忆更新显式执行，不隐藏在自定义 backward 内。


[Unsupervised Feature Learning via Non-Parametric Instance Discrimination](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.01978) · [Official implementation](https://github.com/zhirongw/lemniscate.pytorch/blob/master/lib/NCECriterion.py)

## 小实验与阈值

六个六维归一化实例向量执行 80 次 SGD，学习率 `.35`，T=`.2`，固定 Z=`exp(5)+5`，记忆动量 `.95`。每次枚举另外五个合成实例作为噪声候选，是确定性教学日程，并非复现原始随机采样。实验调用两个待实现函数；T3 要求损失低于 `.8` 且低于初值的 40%，查询与自身记忆平均余弦大于 `.99`，记忆保持单位长度且无梯度。没有图像编码器或下游指标复现。

数据和初始化均为确定性；测试 fixture 还将 Python、NumPy、PyTorch 的种子设为 42。原生标定环境为 Apple silicon 上仓库固定的 PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU。NumPy 自动微分适配器与导出的 WASM 包运行同一套完整训练测试。断言证明本合成任务上的数值和学习行为，不代表论文基准复现。

## 错误实现检查

以下每个 mutant 仅隔离一种错误，完整说明对应题面约定：

- 以 InfoNCE softmax 替代原始 binary NCE。
- 把 K/N 噪声先验错写成 1/N。
- 让历史记忆条目接收自动微分梯度。
- 对 K 个噪声项求平均而非求和。
- 交换 EMA 的新旧权重。
- 存储未归一化的 EMA 条目。
- 忽略固定的配分常数 Z。

来源：[论文](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.01978) 与 [官方代码](https://github.com/zhirongw/lemniscate.pytorch/blob/master/lib/NCECriterion.py)。

原生参考解实测：initial_loss=2.34368; final_loss=0.661522; initial_alignment=0.574979; final_alignment=0.999562。

当非零 EMA 混合向量短于调用者给定的 epsilon 时，必须除以该 epsilon。固定使用 1e-12 会改变合法非默认输入的结果，专门的 mutant 与独立标量用例覆盖此边界。

momentum=1 的快捷路径不能返回输入别名：选中的非单位行仍需归一化，修改返回结果的任意行都不能影响原记忆库。

en.title: Instance Discrimination: Binary NCE and Memory Bank
en.readme:
# Instance Discrimination: Binary NCE and Memory Bank


## 1. Problem


Implement `instance_nce_loss` and `update_memory` for the original non-parametric instance-discrimination method. Every training image has a persistent bank row. The current query is contrasted against a positive instance and sampled noise entries. This paper uses binary noise-contrastive estimation; candidate-softmax InfoNCE is a different objective.


## 2. Core equations


For query $q_b$, candidate IDs $j_{bt}$, fixed partition constant $Z>0$, temperature $T>0$, and $K$ noise draws from $N$ bank rows,
$$a_{bt}=q_b^T v_{j_{bt}}/T-\log Z-\log(K/N),$$
$$L=\frac1B\sum_b\left[\operatorname{softplus}(-a_{b0})+\sum_{t=1}^{K}\operatorname{softplus}(a_{bt})\right].$$
The positive is column zero. Each binary classifier distinguishes the model likelihood from uniform noise. When all $a=0$, loss is $(K+1)\log2$. Update a selected row by $v_i\leftarrow\operatorname{normalize}(m v_i+(1-m)q_i)$.


## 3. Equations to code


Gather bank rows with `memory.detach()`, compute dot products, and work in the log domain to avoid exponential overflow. Sum the K negative terms and average only over B. Do not drop `log_z` or replace `K/N` with `1/N`. Unlike softmax, shifting all model log-likelihoods changes binary NCE. Return an independent detached bank copy after indexed EMA and normalization.


## 4. Exercise conventions


Queries `[B,D]`, bank `[N,D]`, candidate IDs `[B,K+1]`, K≥1. Floats are finite float32/64; IDs are int64 and in range on the same device. Features normally come from a normalized encoder, but this function consumes their supplied values without additional normalization. `log_z` is a fixed finite Python scalar; the paper/official code estimate Z once, which is outside this exercise. Uniform noise draws may repeat and may hit the positive ID. Memory gradients stop; query gradients remain. Memory updates require distinct IDs, momentum in `[0,1]`, and norm floor `eps=1e-12`; untouched rows stay exactly unchanged and zero mixtures remain zero.


At momentum one, selected rows are still normalized; the return always has independent storage, even when no numerical update is needed.

## 5. Interactive plots and CPU lab


Train six normalized six-dimensional instance vectors for 80 SGD steps at learning rate `.35`, using T=`.2`, fixed Z=`exp(5)+5` and bank momentum `.95`. All five other toy IDs are deterministic negative candidates; this schedule illustrates the objective and is not the original stochastic sampler. The lab invokes both submitted functions. T3 requires loss below `.8` and 40% of its initial value, own-bank cosine above `.99`, and unit, detached bank rows. No image encoder or downstream benchmark is reproduced.


## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Extensions and sources


Compare InfoNCE candidate classification with this calibrated binary data-versus-noise classifier. Compare MoCo: MoCo uses a momentum-updated encoder and FIFO queue, whereas this method updates persistent rows addressed by dataset instance ID. The stable log-domain formula here is algebraically the binary NCE objective; it omits the official probability-space denominator’s tiny implementation epsilon to avoid changing calibrated probabilities. The bank update is explicit after the optimizer step rather than hidden in a custom backward operation.


[Unsupervised Feature Learning via Non-Parametric Instance Discrimination](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.01978) · [Official implementation](https://github.com/zhirongw/lemniscate.pytorch/blob/master/lib/NCECriterion.py)

# Implementation notes

Read these after attempting the exercise.

Gather bank rows with `memory.detach()`, compute dot products, and work in the log domain to avoid exponential overflow. Sum the K negative terms and average only over B. Do not drop `log_z` or replace `K/N` with `1/N`. Unlike softmax, shifting all model log-likelihoods changes binary NCE. Return an independent detached bank copy after indexed EMA and normalization.

Queries `[B,D]`, bank `[N,D]`, candidate IDs `[B,K+1]`, K≥1. Floats are finite float32/64; IDs are int64 and in range on the same device. Features normally come from a normalized encoder, but this function consumes their supplied values without additional normalization. `log_z` is a fixed finite Python scalar; the paper/official code estimate Z once, which is outside this exercise. Uniform noise draws may repeat and may hit the positive ID. Memory gradients stop; query gradients remain. Memory updates require distinct IDs, momentum in `[0,1]`, and norm floor `eps=1e-12`; untouched rows stay exactly unchanged and zero mixtures remain zero.

The maintained mutations isolate these faults:

- Use candidate softmax instead of original binary NCE.
- Use 1/N instead of K/N noise prior.
- Let the persistent memory receive autograd gradients.
- Average the noise terms rather than summing them.
- Swap old/new weights in the memory EMA.
- Store unnormalized EMA rows.
- Ignore the fixed partition constant.

## Actual CPU calibration

Train six normalized six-dimensional instance vectors for 80 SGD steps at learning rate `.35`, using T=`.2`, fixed Z=`exp(5)+5` and bank momentum `.95`. All five other toy IDs are deterministic negative candidates; this schedule illustrates the objective and is not the original stochastic sampler. The lab invokes both submitted functions. T3 requires loss below `.8` and 40% of its initial value, own-bank cosine above `.99`, and unit, detached bank rows. No image encoder or downstream benchmark is reproduced.

All data and initial parameters are deterministic; the test fixture also seeds Python/NumPy/PyTorch to 42. Native calibration uses the repository's PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU environment on Apple silicon. Tests use the same full training loop in the NumPy autograd adapter and exported WASM bundle. The gates validate numerical behavior and learning on this synthetic task, not a published paper benchmark.

Source: [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.01978) and [official implementation](https://github.com/zhirongw/lemniscate.pytorch/blob/master/lib/NCECriterion.py).

Observed native reference metrics: initial_loss=2.34368; final_loss=0.661522; initial_alignment=0.574979; final_alignment=0.999562.

A nonzero EMA mixture shorter than the supplied epsilon must be divided by that epsilon. Fixing the norm floor at 1e-12 silently changes valid nondefault inputs; the dedicated mutant and scalar case cover this.

The momentum-one shortcut must not return an alias. Selected non-unit rows still need normalization, and editing any result row must leave the input bank unchanged.
